speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; could you tell me how long these symptoms have been present? Additionally, do you recall any recent insect bites, travel, or contact with animals?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Borrelia burgdorferi infection)

The combination of recent Minnesota camping exposure, migratory joint pain (knee), and now a warm, swollen wrist with systemic symptoms like fever and chills is highly suggestive of early disseminated Lyme arthritis. I would like to confirm the wrist lesion characteristics and check for other specific signs.

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP, and Lyme Serology (IFA).
REQUEST IMAGES: Wrist physical exam photo to assess for erythema and swelling.
